Judgment Total Duration : Year Months Days  02 10 07  JUDGMENT

The petitioner filed this petition under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989 for claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/-.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is that, on 04- 03-2022 at about 11.00 a.m., the petitioner was crossing the Dr. Marigowda Road near Forum Mall, wherein the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05/KR-6382 drove it, in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangerous to human life, came from Tavarekere Junction towards Madiwala Check Post at high speed and dashed against the petitioner, caused the accident, due to forced impact, petitioner fell down, meanwhile the driver of one Auto Rickshaw which was coming behind the said motorcycle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, came at high speed first dashed against the road median and further got turtle and fell on the petitioner and due to which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Anand Kumar.D vs Ramakrishna on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95096364/
2 3.
Immediately, the petitioner was taken to St. John's Hospital, wherein he was treated as an inpatient for 2 days.

During hospitalization X-rays were taken which revealed that the petitioner had sustained medial condyle fracture of right tibia and other injuries and the doctors suggested for the surgery but, due to financial problem petitioner got discharged from the said hospital and went to Naati treatment at Putturu

, since, he was getting more pain again he went to MTB Hospital on 11-03-2022 and was treated an inpatient and on 12-03-202 he had undergone surgery of medial condyle fracture of right tibia ORIF with plate, screws and bone grating under spinal anaesthesia and was discharged on 14-03-2022 with an advice of regular follow up treatment and medication.
As per the advice of the Doctor petitioner is taking regular follow up treatment by spending huge amount of Rs.2,50,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment, food, transport and other charges.

4. Due to injuries sustained in the said accident, petitioner is not able to sit, squat, run jump, walk and is undergoing deep mental shock, pain and sufferings, since the injuries caused are permanent in nature and he is not able to use Indian toilet, he has become complete bed ridden, he is not able to do his routine work and he is depending upon another person for his day to day activities, He is not able to concentrate his work.

5. It is further stated that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 42 years and was working as Driver at Maruthi Playwood, Koramangala, Bangalore and earning Rs.25,000/-per month, he is the only earning member of the family.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is not able to do his work as doing earlier, lost his earning capacity and also facing great financial difficulties.

It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05/ KR-6382 and Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-02/AE- 9471 against whom the Madiwala Traffic Police have registered the case in Crime No.18/2022 punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.

Hence, respondent No.1 being the owner of the motorcycle, respondent No.2 being the owner of the Auto-rickshaw, respondent No.3 being the insurer of the motorcycle and respondent No.4 being the insurer of the Auto-rickshaw are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, prayed to allow the petition.
6. On service of notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 are not appeared before the Court hence, they placed as exparte.
The respondent No.3 and 4 entered appearance through their respective counsels and they have filed separate written statements.
7. The respondent No.3 in its written statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.
The respondent No.1 has denied the age, income and occupation of the petitioner and also the amount spent towards medical expenses by the petitioner.

The respondent No.3 has contended that the insured has violated the terms and conditions of the M.V. Act and the insured and jurisdictional police have not intimated about the alleged accident to the insurer, this respondent has no knowledge about the said accident till served with the notice by this Court.

It is further contended that the driver of the Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-02/AE-9471 was not holding the valid and effective DL at the time of accident and the Anand Kumar.D vs Ramakrishna on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95096364/
3 respondent No.2 by knowingly well willfully used the auto in public place and has contravened the proviso of MV Act and committed the breach of the terms and conditions of the policy.

The alleged accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner alone, who was trying to cross the busy road unmindfully and without having proper lookout and observing the vehicular movements and suddenly came to the middle of the road by running, where there is no provision for pedestrians to cross the road near the place of accident and he came to contact with the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05/KR-6382 and sustained injuries, the accident took place by the negligence of petitioner and rider of the motorcycle and the accident did not take place due to the rash and negligence and involvement of the Auto bearing Reg.No.KA-02/AE-9471 as alleged, as such the petition is to be dismissed against the respondent No.3 as the said Auto did not caused the alleged accident.

This respondent has issued a policy of insurance in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of Auto bearing Reg.No.KA-02/AE-9471 the liability of this respondent company if any is limited to the terms and conditions of the policy and subject to valid and effective driving licence of the driver in question and permit and fitness certificate as per MV Act.
It has further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.
8. The respondent No.4 in its written statement has contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is vexatious and frivolous, it is contrary to law and facts of the case.

It is further contended that he has denied the policy issued in respect of the vehicle motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05/KR-6382 with this respondent and it has not at all issued the policy and hence, this respondent is not a necessary party to the said proceedings.

Respondent No.4 has further contended that there is no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05/KR- 6382, as per the police documents it is clear that Dr. Marigowda Road is two way road of 30 feet each, where vehicle movement are more, petitioner without observing the vehicles, where there is no permissible crossing, he attempted to cross the said road, the rider of the motorcycle tried to stop his vehicle he could not do and he also fell down with the said vehicle, the driver of Auto-rickshaw who was coming back went and dashed against the center median and turtle fell on the petitioner.
The police documents supports the same, if the petitioner would have little careful he would have avoided the said unforeseen situation, the entire negligence is on the part of the petitioner.
The rider of the said motorcycle was not having valid DL as on the date of the alleged accident.
It has further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Except these things, all other averments made in the petition are denied by this respondent and hence, on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.
9. Based on the pleadings, following issues are framed:-

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 04- 03-2022 at about 11.00 a.m., the petitioner was crossing the Dr. Marigowda Road, near Forum Mall,
at that time one Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05/KR- Anand Kumar.D vs Ramakrishna on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95096364/
4 6382 drove in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering human life, came from Tavarekere Junction towards Madiwala Check Post at a high speed and dashed against the petitioner.

As a result of forced impact, the petitioner fell down, meanwhile one Auto Rickshaw which was coming behind the Motorcycle drove by rash and negligent manner, came at high speed first dashed against the road median and further got turtle and fell on the petitioner and sustained grievous injuries?

2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
3) What order or award?
10. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P1 to 18.
The respondent No.4 got examined its Legal Manager as RW.1 and got marked the documents as per Ex.R.1 and 2.
The respondent No.3 got examined Senior Executive-Claims Legal as RW.2 and got marked at Ex.R.3 to 6 and 6(a).

11. Heard the arguments.
12.

My findings on the above issues as under:-
Issue No.1 ... In the affirmative, Issue No.2 ... Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.3 ...

As per final order For the following:
REASONS 13. POINT No.1: The petitioner filed this petition against the respondents for claiming compensation due to injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident, that occurred on 04-03-2022.
14.
In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and reiterated the averments of petition in his chief-examination affidavit and got marked 14 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.

Ex.P.1 is the copy of FIR, Ex.P.2 is the copy of first information, Ex.P.3 is the copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the copy of sketch, Ex.P.5 is the copy of IMV report, Ex.P.6 is the copy of Wound Certificate, Ex.P.7 is the copy of notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act, Ex.P.8 is the reply to 133 notice,
Ex.P.9 is the copy of charge sheet, Ex.P.10 is the discharge summary, Ex.P.11 is the copy of Aadhar Card of the petitioner, Ex.P.12 is the copy of DL, Ex.P.13 is the medical bills, Ex.P.14 is the medical prescriptions.
In the cross-examination of PW.1, he has denied that, at Forum Signals there is option to cross the road by way of skywalk.

Further stated that, he was crossed more than 50% of the road,
at that time signal was opened and Auto and Bike came at high speed and hit him.
Further denied that he wrongly crossed the road and obstructed bike and auto and accident caused due to his negligence.
15. The petitioner is examined the MRO of Medical Records Department, MTB Hospital, Bengaluru as PW.2 and got marked 02 documents as Ex.P.15 and P.16.

Ex.P.15 is the authorization letter,
Ex.P.16 is the discharge summary.

In cross examination nothing worthy has been elicited to Anand Kumar.D vs Ramakrishna on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95096364/
5 disbelieve his evidence and documents produced by him.
16.

sentences.text: The petitioner also examined the Orthopaedic Surgeon of SOADS as PW.3 and got marked 02 documents as Ex.P.17 and P.18.
Ex.P.17 is the clinical notes and Ex.P.18 is the X- ray.
In the cross-examination of PW.3, he has deposed that, he is not the treated doctor, fractures are united and implants are not removed.
Further denied that the disability can only be assessed after removal of implants and he has given higher disability.
17. On the other hand, the respondent No.4 got examined its Manager Legal as RW.1 and got marked 02 documents as Ex.R.1 is the Authorization Letter and Ex.R.2 is the Insurance Policy.
RW.1 in his chief-examination has stated that, the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05/KR-6382 was insured with respondent No.4 and it was valid on the date of accident.
Further stated that the accident was not took place due to the negligent driving of the driver of their insured vehicle.
In the cross-examination of RW.1 has denied that, he is deposing falsely to avoid the compensation.

18. The respondent No.3 got examined its Senior Executive- Claims Legal as RW.2 and got marked 04 documents as per Ex.R.3 is the authorization letter, Ex.R.4 is the Insurance Policy, Ex.R.5 is the notice issued to respondent No.1, Ex.R.6 is the un-served postal cover and Ex.R.6(a) if the copy of notice in Ex.R.6.
In the cross-examination of RW.2 has denied that, she is deposing falsely to avoid the compensation.

19. On perusal of spot sketch and charge sheet, it appears that, on the date of accident, the driver of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05/KR-6382 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangerous to human life, came from Tavarekere Junction towards Madiwala Check Post at high speed and dashed against the petitioner, caused the accident due to forced impact, petitioner fell down, meanwhile the driver of one Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-02/AE-9471 was coming behind the said motorcycle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, came at high speed first dashed against the road median and further got turtle and fell on the petitioner.
As a result of which, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Hence, the Madivala Police have filed charge sheet against drivers of both offending vehicles for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
20.
Therefore it is clear that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the drivers of the both offending vehicles.
For the purpose of disproving the sole negligence of the drivers of the Motorcycle and Autorickshaw, nothing has been eliciting from the mouth of the petitioner.

Further,
the owners of offending vehicles have not challenged the charge sheet.

21. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioner has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.
22.

sentences.text:
The respondent No.4 in its written statement has denied the issuance of policy to the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05/KR-6382, but officer of respondent No.4 examined as RW.1 has Anand Kumar.D vs Ramakrishna on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95096364/
6 clearly admitted the issuance of policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, it is clear that the respondent No.4 has issued a policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05/KR-6382 and it was valid and in force as on the date of accident.
23.

The respondent No.3 and 4 took contention that the respondent No.1 and 2 have violated the policy terms and conditions, but the respondent No.3 and 4 have not produced oral or documentary evidence to prove its contention.
There is nothing on record to show that the respondent No.1 and 2 have violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, this Court is of considered opinion that the respondent No.3 and 4 have not proved that the respondent No.1 and 2 have violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

24. After careful scrutiny of Ex.P.1 is the copy of FIR, Ex.P.2 is the copy of first information, Ex.P.3 is the copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the copy of sketch, Ex.P.5 is the copy of IMV report, Ex.P.6 is the copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.7 is the copy of notice U/Sec.133 of Indian Evidence Act, Ex.P.8 is the reply of 133 notice, Ex.P.9 is the copy of charge sheet, it appears that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05/KR-6382 and also the driver of the Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-02/AE-9471.
25.
On perusal of entire materials on record, it appears that the offending motorcycle and offending Auto-rickshaw have equally contributed in the accident.
If both the vehicles have taken the proper precautions, then, the accident could have been avoided.
Therefore, the offending motorcycle and autorickshaw had equal involvement in the said accident.
Hence, both the vehicles had equal contributory negligence.
Accordingly, equal contributory negligence is taken on the part of the rider and driver of both the vehicles.
Therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that both the vehicles are equally contributed their negligence in the accident.

Accordingly, apportion of the negligence on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle Reg.No.KA-05/KR-6382 is taken at 50% and on the driver of autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-02/AE-9471 is taken at 50%.
Hence, this Tribunal answers the Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
26. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner is claiming the compensation amount of Rs.20,00,000/- with respect to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

The petitioner produced Ex.P.6 wound certificate issued by St. John's Medical College Hospital, Bangalore and Ex.P.10 discharge summary issued by MTB Orthopaedic & Trauma Hospital, Bangalore and prayed to award compensation amount.

entities.text: St. John's Medical College Hospital, Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Respondents not disputed the said documents.

On perusal of the Wound Certificate, it discloses that the petitioner has sustained the following injuries:
1) Swelling and tenderness over right knee, CT right knee, right tibia medial condyle fracture, right fibula head fracture.
2) Multiple Abrasions of various sizes, over back, left forearm, chest and right blank region.
The doctor has opined that the injury No.1 is grievous in nature and injury No.2 is simple in nature.

Therefore, taking all these facts and nature of injuries, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner Anand Kumar.D vs Ramakrishna on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95096364/
7 is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
27. As per the medical bills and prescriptions marked as per Ex.P.13 and 14 the petitioner has spent Rs.1,95,474/- towards medical expenses.
The respondents not denied the medical bills.

On perusal of the said medical bills and also considering the bills and also treatment taken by the petitioner in the hospital, the petitioner is entitled to claim the medical bills amount of Rs.1,95,475/- under the head of medical expenditure.
28. The petitioner not produced any documents with respect to expenditure of transportation, food and other charges.
However, the petitioner produced one Discharge Summary issued by MTB Orthopedic & Trauma Hospital, Bangalore which is marked as Ex.P.10.
It discloses that, the petitioner took treatment inpatient in the said hospital from 11-03-2022 to 14-03-2022 i.e., for about 04 days.

Therefore, considering the treatment taken as inpatient in the hospital, this tribunal has award reasonable compensation of Rs.4,000/- under the head transportation, nourishment and conveyance charges.
29. The Petitioner contended that, due to injuries he was suffering from pain and mental agony and he is unable to carry on his day to day activities which he used to do prior to the accident.
To prove the assessment of disability, the petitioner got examined one Doctor Sri. Nagaraj B.N. as PW- 3.
In the chief examination affidavit PW.3 deposed that, on 10-01-2022 the petitioner came to him for assessment of disability purpose and sustained right medial tibial condyle fracture.

As per the medical reports he was initially treated at St. John's Hospital and as per the copy of Discharge summary the petitioner was operated at MTB Hospital with ORIF with plate and screws on 12-03-2022 and later discharged on 14-03-2022 and he was on regular follow up in the same hospital and the fractures are united.

The petitioner complains of weakness and pain in the right knee, unable to sit down, squat and sit cross leg and he has healed keloid scar over the right proximal leg, restricted right knee movements, wasting of the right thigh muscles and the recent X-ray of the right leg shows united tibial condyle fracture with implant in situ.
He examined clinically and radiologically and further assessed the total physical disability of the right lower limb at 43% and that of to the whole body disability of the petitioner at 14%.

In the cross- examination admitted that, personally he had not treated the petitioner and further denied that the fractures are united and implant are not removed and also denied that permanent disability can be assessed only after removal of implant and without removal of implants assessment of disability is premature and he assessed only physical disability and also denied that he has deposing falsely that, there is loss of 52 degree to range of movement of knee and he had given false point to stability component to help the petitioner.
Further he denied that he had given additional point to deformity in functional position and had given higher side of disability of 14% to whole body to help the petitioner.
However by considering the nature of the wound, condition of the petitioner and evidence of the doctor this Tribunal has considered the disability of the petitioner at 10% to the whole body.
30. The petitioner stated that, at the time of accident he was aged about 42 years and he was working as Driver at Maruthi Playwood, Koramangala, Bangalore and was earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
Anand Kumar.

D vs Ramakrishna on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95096364/
8 and due to accidental injuries he is not able to do his work as before the accident.
The petitioner has not produced any documents to prove his income and avocation.
In present days the Coolie worker get Rs.500/- to Rs.600/- per day.

However by considering the age and occupation of petitioner this Tribunal taken the monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.15,500/-.
31.
As per Ex.P.11 and P.12 Notarized Copy of Adhar Card and D.L. date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 1980 and 03-03-1980 respectively.
Therefore, age of the petitioner is taken as 42 years at the time of accident.

Then the proper multiplier applicable is 14 which comes as follows:
Rs.15,500 x 12 x 14 x 10% = Rs.2,60,400/-
Hence, this Tribunal has award Rs.2,60,400/- under the head loss of future earning capacity on account of disability.
32. The petitioner also sought for expenses towards future medicine for further treatment.
In the chief-examination affidavit the petitioner deposed that, he is forced to spent huge amount for future medication.
The PW.3 doctor deposed in the chief affidavit that, the petitioner needs another surgery for the removal of implant and the estimate of said surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
In the Cross examination the PW.3 admitted that he had not treated the petitioner and fractures are united and implants are not removed.
However, by considering the age and nature of injury and evidence of the doctor, this Tribunal has award reasonable compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head future medical expenses.
(Which does not carry any interest).

33. The Petitioner stated that, prior to the accident he was aged about 42 years and he was working as Driver at Maruthi Playwood, Koramangala, Bangalore and was earning Rs.25,000/- p.m. and due to injuries sustained in the accident, he is unable to attend the work and facing financial difficulties.
The Petitioner had not produced any document to prove his income and avocation.
This accident occurred in the year 2022.

However by considering the age and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal awarded reasonable compensation amount of Rs.30,000/- under the head loss of income during laid up period.
34. The petitioner sustained grievous injury as shown in the wound certificate.
The petitioner was working as Driver at Maruthi Playwood, Koramangala, Bangalore and due to accidental injuries his routine work was hampered for some days.

Therefore, by considering this aspect and the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal awarded the amount of Rs.30,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of loss of amenities.

35. Considering oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence, it is just and proper to grant compensation as follows:
 Under the Heads Amount  1. Pain and sufferings Rs. 40,000/-
 2. Medical expenses Rs. 1,95,474/-
 3. Transportation, Nourishment, 4,000/-
 Conveyance and attendant charges.

9  4. Loss of future income on account of 2,60,400/-
Permanent disability

5. Towards future medical expenses Rs. 40,000/-
 6. Loss of income during laidup period.

Rs. 30,000/-
 7. Towards loss of amenities of life Rs. 30,000/-
The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,99,874/-, which is rounded off to Rs.6,00,000/-.
36. Interest:

In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru has held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest that can be awarded on Judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a. and that since Sec.149 of M.V. Act provides for the interest on Judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a.
(Excluding the future medical expenses) and not more than that.

entities.text: Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.

37. Liability:-
As already observed above, Respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.4 is the insurer of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05/KR-6382 and respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the Insurer Authorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-02/AE-9471.

As discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the drivers of both offending vehicles,
hence Respondent No.1 to 4 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Further the respondent No.3 and 4 being Insurers of both the offending vehicles are primarily held liable to pay the compensation amount at the apportionment at 50% each with interest to the petitioner.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answered Issue No.2 in the Partly Affirmative.

38. Issue No.3: for the foregoing reasons, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost as hereunder.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.6,00,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a., (Excluding future medical expenses of Rs.40,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.

10
The Respondent No.1 to 4 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Further, Respondent No.3 being Insurer of the offending vehicle of Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit at the ratio of 50%, Respondent No.4 being Insurer of the offending vehicle of Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit at the ratio of 50% of the compensation amount, together with 6% interest within 60 days, from the date of this order.

After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner (As the petitioner has incurred huge amount towards medical expenses and also he is a need for future medical expenses) with proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
As a result of which, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Hence, the Madivala Police have filed charge sheet against drivers of both offending vehicles for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
20.
Therefore it is clear that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the drivers of the both offending vehicles.
For the purpose of disproving the sole negligence of the drivers of the Motorcycle and Autorickshaw, nothing has been eliciting from the mouth of the petitioner.
Further,
the owners of offending vehicles have not challenged the charge sheet.
21. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioner has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.
22.
Therefore, it is clear that the respondent No.4 has issued a policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05/KR-6382 and it was valid and in force as on the date of accident.
23.
The respondent No.3 and 4 took contention that the respondent No.1 and 2 have violated the policy terms and conditions, but the respondent No.3 and 4 have not produced oral or documentary evidence to prove its contention.
There is nothing on record to show that the respondent No.1 and 2 have violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, this Court is of considered opinion that the respondent No.3 and 4 have not proved that the respondent No.1 and 2 have violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
On perusal of entire materials on record, it appears that the offending motorcycle and offending Auto-rickshaw have equally contributed in the accident.
If both the vehicles have taken the proper precautions, then, the accident could have been avoided.
Therefore, the offending motorcycle and autorickshaw had equal involvement in the said accident.
Hence, both the vehicles had equal contributory negligence.
Accordingly, equal contributory negligence is taken on the part of the rider and driver of both the vehicles.
Therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that both the vehicles are equally contributed their negligence in the accident.
In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru has held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest that can be awarded on Judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a. and that since Sec.149 of M.V. Act provides for the interest on Judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a.
(Excluding the future medical expenses) and not more than that.
As discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the drivers of both offending vehicles,
hence Respondent No.1 to 4 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

35. Considering oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence, it is just and proper to grant compensation as follows:
 Under the Heads Amount  1. Pain and sufferings Rs. 40,000/-
 2. Medical expenses Rs. 1,95,474/-
 3. Transportation, Nourishment, 4,000/-
 Conveyance and attendant charges.
Permanent disability
Rs. 30,000/-
 7. Towards loss of amenities of life Rs. 30,000/-
The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,99,874/-, which is rounded off to Rs.6,00,000/-.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
Further the respondent No.3 and 4 being Insurers of both the offending vehicles are primarily held liable to pay the compensation amount at the apportionment at 50% each with interest to the petitioner.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answered Issue No.2 in the Partly Affirmative.
38. Issue No.3: for the foregoing reasons, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost as hereunder.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.6,00,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a., (Excluding future medical expenses of Rs.40,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 to 4 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further, Respondent No.3 being Insurer of the offending vehicle of Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit at the ratio of 50%, Respondent No.4 being Insurer of the offending vehicle of Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit at the ratio of 50% of the compensation amount, together with 6% interest within 60 days, from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner (As the petitioner has incurred huge amount towards medical expenses and also he is a need for future medical expenses) with proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
